verdict:
V2D attempt 1: ACCEPTED WITH CONDITIONS. Reviewer: external (operator relay).
S0 to S3 and G1 to G5 are accepted. The S4 G4 stop was correct: the V2D prompt
defined C-SIMPLE as a deterministic threshold, which cannot match a fractional
escape rate when standard trajectories are identical. This is recorded as a
reviewer design defect, not an implementation failure. The pooled E3
validation is accepted. The relative x/z brain map with disclosed unverified
units and orientation is accepted. Bot results are development evidence only.
Conditions for V2E:
F1 C-SIMPLE becomes a stochastic one-neuron baseline (defined in V2E).
F2 Pilot observation: in dry run 3 at s = 0.039, every pilot null (2 per family
   per circuit) exceeded 96 Hz whole-circuit no-threat rate while the real T1a
   and T1b graphs stayed below 20 Hz. This motivates a new confirmatory
   hypothesis H0 (dynamic stability), tested only on fresh nulls. The pilot
   nulls are excluded. H0 is disclosed as pilot-motivated.
F3 A sign-stratified null family N-SIGN is added.
F4 Primary-circuit fallback rule for H1 and H2 (no real T1a subset point passed
   in dry run 3; one real T1b point passed).
F5 The game must use a calibrated point; provisional-model issues: the fly
   never escaped and barely moved, the hand was not visible in the mid-strike
   capture, the board is not the hero on phones, brain-cam flashes are faint,
   and the repository has no README.
